t: They say food appeared when the stores were nearly bare. The god heard us.
I heard supplies appeared without anyone bringing them. That sounds like help.
Someone found food and forgot who placed it. That is hardly proof.
Word reached us that food appeared in another settlement's empty stores.
The account says the god filled every basket before dawn.
Farther on, they claim food came from nowhere. I hope some part is true.
The story crossed two settlements and gained a feast along the way.
I have told it often: the stores were empty, then the god provided.
They say a wound closed beneath the god's attention.
I heard someone recovered suddenly. Maybe the god helped the healing along.
A healer treated the wound, and later people credited the god.
A distant account says a dying person stood up healed.
They speak beyond the hills of flesh restored by divine mercy.
The healing story sounds larger each time it travels.
By the time the account reached us, a scratch had become mortal.
I still tell how the wound closed while we watched.
They say the ground shook when the god's anger passed beneath it.
I heard dishes fell and walls shifted. Maybe the god moved below them.
Ground moves sometimes. Fear supplied the divine explanation afterward.
People beyond the ridge report a shaking strong enough to wake every house.
The distant account says the god made the whole valley kneel.
The shaking may have been divine. The broken walls were certainly real.
Each village adds another fallen building to the earthquake account.
I have repeated the shaking so often I remember people's faces best.
They say the god drove the wolf away after it mauled someone.
I heard someone survived a wolf attack. Perhaps prayer helped.
A wolf attacked someone, and frightened neighbours made it divine.
News came from another settlement that wolves took a person near the trees.
They say the god spared someone from a whole pack beyond the ridge.
The far account cannot decide whether the person lived.
One wolf became five before the story reached our fire.
I keep telling where the wolf came from so others watch that path.
They say the god called someone away before their family was ready.
I heard someone died suddenly. I do not know whether there was meaning.
A person died, and grief made every ordinary detail sound divine.
Word came from far away that a person died without warning.
The distant account says the god took someone in full view of the village.
I heard a death became a warning after several tellings.
Nobody who tells the story knew the person who died.
I have told the death often, but I refuse to improve it.
They say the god raised someone until their feet cleared the roof.
I heard a person rose without support. That leaves little room for easy answers.
Someone fell, and the account now begins with them floating.
A story from the next valley has a person rising above the houses.
They say the god lifted someone high enough for every doubter to see.
Perhaps someone truly rose. The height changes with every speaker.
The far account lifts the person higher each time it is told.
I still remember the empty space beneath their feet.
They say the god lowered someone gently after displaying divine power.
I heard a floating person reached the ground unharmed. Maybe mercy ended it.
Someone landed safely, and people invented a divine descent.
The travelling account says a person descended without bending a blade of grass.
They say the god returned someone to earth as gently as sleep.
The safe landing sounds possible. The rest sounds polished by travel.
Nobody remembers who first claimed the person floated before landing.
I tell the landing because everyone asks what happened after the rising.
They say the god slammed someone down hard enough to split the earth.
I heard a person struck the ground without falling first. I cannot settle that.
A person fell hard. The divine force appeared in later accounts.
A distant story says someone hit the ground and shook every nearby wall.
They say the god cast a person down as a public warning.
Something terrible happened when the person landed. The cause remains disputed.
The impact grows louder whenever the story crosses another settlement.
I have repeated the landing, but the sound is what stays with me.
They say the god tore a whole tree from the soil.
I heard a tree rose roots first. Weather seems too easy an answer.
A rotten tree fell, and the story turned the fall upward.
Beyond the ridge, people claim an entire grove left the ground.
The distant account says the god pulled trees out like weeds.
One tree may have moved. A travelling story has made it a forest.
No witness who reached us agrees how many trees moved.
I tell where the roots broke because that part proves what I saw.
They say the god struck a person beneath a cloudless sky.
I heard the bolt came without thunder. That sounds deliberate, though I hesitate.
Lightning killed someone. Clear weather does not prove judgment.
A far settlement tells of a person struck under a bright sky.
They say the god named a sinner with lightning before the whole town.
The strange lightning may be true. The person's supposed guilt may not be.
The farther the account travels, the clearer the dead person's crime becomes.
I repeat only the strike. I never claim to know the reason.
They say the god made bare ground produce a season's growth in moments.
I heard the field changed before anyone could explain it.
A good field became a miracle after enough people discussed it.
News from beyond the hills says empty land turned green overnight.
The distant account credits the god with feeding an entire settlement at once.
Somewhere far away, a field changed suddenly. I would like to see it.
The crop doubles each time the account moves down the road.
I keep telling how quickly the shoots appeared, though nobody believes the timing.
They say the god threw someone beyond the village path.
I heard a person flew without being touched. I cannot dismiss that easily.
Someone was knocked down, and every teller adds another body length.
The far account has someone flying from one settlement to the next.
They say the god flung a person so all nearby settlements would hear.
A person may truly have flown. The distance is now anybody's guess.
The story throws them farther because nobody checks where they landed.
I have told the throw many times. I still leave out the screaming.
They say a safe child was born after prayers from the whole house.
I heard both survived a difficult birth. That leaves room for hope.
A healer delivered a healthy child. The prayer story arrived later.
A travelling account tells of a child born safely after a terrible night.
